content.user_title: Compare Job Offers with Levels.fyi Pay Data
content.value_statement: Different vesting schedules and signing bonuses make job offers difficult to compare. This skill normalizes compensation and compares each offer with its company and level median.
actual_capabilities: Collect missing offer details, including base pay, stock grants, vesting schedules, bonuses, signing payments, and relocation.
Calculate normalized yearly compensation, first-year compensation, and four-year totals using the specified formulas.
Convert non-USD offers to USD using an explicitly approximate exchange rate.
Retrieve company levels and compensation medians through Levels.fyi tools, then show each offer's gap from its level median.
Present side-by-side comparisons highlighting cash, equity, vesting differences, and compensation leaders.
Offer an optional salary contribution through a companion skill after asking the user.
limitations: Live benchmarks require Levels.fyi tool access; access setup and salary contributions depend on companion skills.
Stock options are listed without valuation, and unpromised equity refreshers are excluded.
Free data lacks level-specific percentiles, sample sizes, and base, stock, and bonus breakdowns.
The comparison is not financial advice and does not assess non-pay factors unless requested.

use_cases.title: Compare competing offers
use_cases.description: Compare cash, equity, signing payments, and vesting schedules across employers using consistent compensation measures.

use_cases.title: Evaluate a counteroffer
use_cases.description: Compare a counteroffer with an external offer and current annual stock compensation to understand the pay differences.

use_cases.title: Review an international move
use_cases.description: Convert offers to approximate USD values and compare compensation against each employer's level median.
use_cases.target_user: Professionals considering offers in different currencies

prompt_templates.title: Start an offer comparison
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare my offers from [company A] and [company B]. Ask for missing compensation details one or two questions at a time.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: collect the information needed for a comparison.

prompt_templates.title: Compare complete packages
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare these offers: [offer details]. Show yearly compensation, first-year compensation, four-year totals, and each company's median for the offered level.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: compare offers with known compensation details.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate a counteroffer
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare my current job, counteroffer, and external offer: [details]. Use current annual stock compensation for my job. Highlight cash, equity, and vesting differences.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: compare an existing role with competing packages.

prompt_templates.title: Compare currencies and vesting
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare these three offers: [details, currencies, vesting schedules]. State approximate USD conversion rates. Show compensation totals and benchmark gaps. Keep company lookups within the skill's limits.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: compare international offers with different vesting schedules.

output_examples.input: Compare two USD offers with even four-year vesting. A: $150,000 base, $100,000 stock grant, $15,000 annual bonus, $20,000 first-year signing payment. B: $160,000 base, $80,000 stock grant, $10,000 annual bonus, no signing payment. Neither includes relocation.
output: Offer A: $195,000 normalized yearly compensation; $210,000 first-year compensation; $780,000 four-year total.
Offer B: $190,000 normalized yearly compensation; $190,000 first-year compensation; $760,000 four-year total.
Offer A leads by $5,000 yearly and $20,000 over four years.
Company and level details are needed for benchmark lookups.
Data: Levels.fyi, medians from the last 12 months.

output_examples.input: Compare first-year pay for two USD offers. Each has $160,000 base, $20,000 annual bonus, and a $160,000 four-year stock grant. A vests 25% yearly with no signing payment. B vests 10%, 20%, 30%, then 40%, with a $30,000 first-year signing payment. Neither includes relocation.
output: Offer A: $40,000 stock vesting in year one and $220,000 first-year compensation.
Offer B: $16,000 stock vesting in year one and $226,000 first-year compensation.
Offer B leads first-year compensation by $6,000 because its signing payment exceeds the initial equity difference.
Normalized yearly compensation is $220,000 for A and $227,500 for B.
Data: Levels.fyi, medians from the last 12 months.

best_practices: Provide the complete stock grant and vesting schedule, and distinguish recurring bonuses from one-time payments.
Include company, role, level, location, currency, and annual stock compensation for any current job.
Review approximate exchange rates and median comparisons before using the results in a compensation discussion.
anti_patterns: Treating a total stock grant as one year of compensation.
Including stock option valuations or unpromised refreshers in the comparison totals.
Choosing an employer solely from compensation totals without considering your own non-pay priorities.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide company, role, level, location, currency, base pay, stock grant, vesting schedule, target bonus, signing payments, and relocation.

faq.question: How is yearly compensation calculated?
faq.answer: It adds base pay, annualized stock, target bonus, and one quarter of signing and relocation payments.

faq.question: How does first-year compensation differ?
faq.answer: It uses stock actually vesting in year one and includes all first-year signing payments and relocation.

faq.question: Can I compare offers in different currencies?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill converts non-USD offers to USD and identifies the exchange rate as approximate.

faq.question: Does free access include detailed compensation distributions?
faq.answer: Free data provides medians, not level-specific percentiles, sample sizes, or pay-component breakdowns. The skill can mention separate Levels.fyi access for those details.

faq.question: Does the skill automatically publish my compensation?
faq.answer: No. It asks whether you want to contribute through a separate skill and offers the option to skip small companies.
